bugs:
Error messages include the raw quantity cell (app/Imports/StockLevelImporter.php:128-129). If a row has non-UTF-8 bytes in quantity (common in Windows-1252 warehouse exports), response()->json throws 'Malformed UTF-8' and returns 500 instead of 200, so the valid rows are never reported to the caller. Probe: "sku,quantity
A,1
B,\xE9
" returned 500.
The too-large check uses strlen($quantity) > 10 (app/Imports/StockLevelImporter.php:129), so a valid whole number with leading zeros such as '00000000005' is rejected as 'too large'.
Reads the file with fgets line by line, so a quoted field containing a newline is split into two rows and both are reported with the wrong column count. All three implementations share this.
antipatterns: app/Imports/StockLevelImporter.php:60-65 sets created_at/updated_at by hand. Eloquent\Builder::upsert already adds the timestamps and puts updated_at in the update columns, so this is redundant.
app/Imports/StockLevelImporter.php:128 puts unvalidated file content into a user-facing message without sanitising it.
app/Imports/StockLevelImporter.php:60 calls now() once per row inside the loop.
strengths: Streams the file with fopen/fgets, closes the handle in try/finally, and flushes upserts in batches of 500, so memory stays bounded.
Thin invokable controller plus a FormRequest using mimes:csv,txt and max:5120. A ValidationException for a missing header gives a proper 422.
Checks the column-count rule against the header width, trims fields, rejects quantities above unsigned int, and caps sku length at 255.
Thorough Pest tests: datasets for missing headers, a precise line-number test, batch-boundary test, oversized file, non-file input, and guest access with and without JSON.

bugs: Reads the file with fgets line by line, so a quoted field containing a newline breaks row and line numbering. All three implementations share this.
antipatterns: app/Actions/ImportStockCsv.php:24-57 builds the whole deduplicated row set in memory and upserts only at the end, rather than flushing while streaming. Memory is bounded by the 5 MB cap, so this is minor.
app/Actions/ImportStockCsv.php:64 returns the header as a positional tuple [$sku, $quantity, $columns], which is less self-describing than a keyed array or a small value object.
strengths: Single-purpose invokable Action, a thin invokable controller named StoreStockImportController, a named route, and a FormRequest with mimes:csv,txt|max:5120.
Relies on Eloquent upsert to manage timestamps (StockLevel::upsert(..., ['quantity'])) and declares an integer cast on the model.
Streams the file with try/finally fclose. Strips the BOM, handles CRLF, uses escape:'' for RFC-style quoting, checks against the header width, and caps sku length and unsigned int range.
Messages never echo raw cell contents, so non-UTF-8 files still return 200 with correct errors. Leading-zero quantities are accepted.
Best test suite: exact line numbers with blank lines, whitespace-only sku, a semicolon delimiter producing 422, PDF/PNG rejection, and both the 5 MB boundary and an over-limit file.

bugs: Treats the first non-blank line as the header (app/Services/StockCsvParser.php:24-41). A file starting with a blank line is accepted with its header on line 2, which contradicts 'the header is line 1'; the other two return 422.

'imported' is count($records), i.e. distinct SKUs (app/Http/Controllers/StockImportController.php:35). A valid row that repeats a SKU is neither counted nor reported as an error, so imported + errors no longer accounts for every row.
Loads the whole upload into memory ($request->file('file')->get()) and then preg_splits it into a second full array (StockImportController.php:15, StockCsvParser.php:17-18). This is not streaming.
Quoted fields containing newlines break, as in the other implementations.
antipatterns: app/Http/Controllers/StockImportController.php:17-32: the controller holds persistence logic (building records, chunked upsert) and turns a null sentinel from the parser into a ValidationException. The responsibilities are split awkwardly across controller and service.
app/Services/StockCsvParser.php:15 returns a nullable array as a sentinel for 'bad header', a weak contract compared with throwing.

app/Http/Controllers/StockImportController.php:27 sets created_at/updated_at by hand, which Eloquent upsert already does. The (string) $sku cast is needed only because numeric SKUs become integer array keys.
Generic App\Services namespace for a single parser. There is no model factory, and tests use StockLevel::create directly.
tests/Feature/StockImportTest.php:95,105,109 assert assertJsonValidationErrors('file') without checking the message.
strengths: The FormRequest pairs extensions:csv with mimetypes:text/csv,text/plain,application/csv, checking both the client extension and the content type, and a test covers binary content renamed to .csv.
Leading zeros are handled (ltrim before the length check) and the unsigned int range is enforced.
Handles bare CR line endings as well as LF and CRLF.
Compact tests that cover the main failure paths, BOM/CRLF, and line numbering with blank lines.

v.rationale: All three suites pass. I read every added file and ran 12 probe cases per implementation, then deleted the probes. impl-2 ranks first. It streams the file, closes the handle in finally, leaves the timestamps to Eloquent upsert, keeps file content out of error messages, accepts leading-zero quantities, and has the most thorough Pest tests, including the 5 MB boundary. Its only real flaw is collecting all deduplicated rows before upserting, which is minor given the 5 MB cap. impl-1 has the best design for memory (it streams and flushes in batches) and equally good tests. But it has a real bug on untrusted input: it echoes the raw quantity cell into the error message, so a non-UTF-8 byte makes the whole import return 500. It also wrongly rejects '00000000005' as too large. impl-3 reads the whole file into memory and splits it into a second array. Its controller does both the persistence and the conversion of the parser's null result into a 422. It accepts a header that is not on line 1, and it counts distinct SKUs as 'imported', so repeated rows disappear from the report. Its upload validation (extension plus content type) is the strictest of the three, but that does not make up for the other problems.
